name: m4-symfinal-stack-pmu
description: Does [retronym/scala#201](https://github.com/retronym/scala/pull/201) at its final head keep the gain measured for the whole of [retronym/scala#199](https://github.com/retronym/scala/pull/199), and do the parts it left behind earn a PR of their own? `m4-symfinal-scala` has only ms, predates the `val`, and is -1.87% ±8.97. `m4-devirt-tip-ab` (-4.09% ±0.64) is the whole of #199 on another base.

A stack on `2.13.x`, full compile of the scala corpus, with cycles and instructions from kperf. `aa` is the base built again, as the floor for the smaller steps. Compare `symfinal` with `base` for #201, `typeparam` and `stranded` with `symfinal` for question 5. Release optimizer settings (`SCALA_RELEASE_OPT`); patched JDK 26, 8G heap, single-shot 4+4 ops.

variantDescriptions.symfinal: retronym/scala#201 at `4636892ff7`: the three source commits, with the `val`, plus MiMa filters and tests
variantDescriptions.stranded: `typeparam` plus the `typeParams` `rawInfo` fast path, `applyFast`, `mapConserveTypes` and the static `SubstMap` branches, all that #201 left out of #199's source (`a9f86b326b`)
